taskVersion.name: pilot-ves-label-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Kor-road, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model from the published survey:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1916 | 1.24 | 1.24
2 | 1252 | 1.79 | 3.03
3 | 1658 | 108 | 111
4 | 581 | - | -

The paper labels this station's curve as HK-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Kor-road, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the paper's curve-type label does not fit the layer values.

Station Kor-road, Bori Metropolis. The subsurface profile consists of four layers. The resistivity sequence begins at 1916 $\Omega\text{m}$ (Layer 1), decreases to 1252 $\Omega\text{m}$ (Layer 2), increases to 1658 $\Omega\text{m}$ (Layer 3), and subsequently decreases to 581 $\Omega\text{m}$ (Layer 4). Evaluating the consecutive triplets for curve-type notation: the first triplet (1916-1252-1658) follows the H pattern ($r_1 > r_2 < r_3$), and the second triplet (1252-1658-581) follows the K pattern ($r_1 < r_2 > r_3$). This results in an HK curve type, which is consistent with the label provided in the published survey.

{"curve_type_stated": "HK", "label_issue_flagged": false}
